chapters.title: Building Wealth
chapters.sourcePressure: The source distinguishes wealth from money and status, then builds a system around specific knowledge, accountability, ownership, leverage, long-term games, judgment, focus, luck, and patience. The pressure is to show wealth as a learned architecture, not a grind.
chapters.coreMove: Convert ambition from rented effort into owned, leveraged specific knowledge that can compound.
chapters.commonMisread: The weak version becomes generic startup advice, hustle culture, passive-income tips, or money motivation without the machinery of ownership, accountability, and permissionless leverage.

chapters.title: Building Judgment
chapters.sourcePressure: The source treats judgment as wisdom applied to external decisions in an age of leverage. Clear thinking requires basics, empty space, mental models, identity shedding, radical honesty, decision heuristics, and reading from first principles.
chapters.coreMove: Strip identity and desire away from a decision until the basic reality can be seen and reasoned from.
chapters.commonMisread: The weak version praises intelligence, contrarian opinions, or mental-model trivia without showing the reader how ego, busyness, and borrowed identities distort decisions.

chapters.title: Learning Happiness
chapters.sourcePressure: The source frames happiness as learned peace: absence of desire, presence, acceptance, lowered identity, fewer vices, and habits that improve the baseline. It rejects success as the price of happiness and treats envy, comparison, and nexting as mental motion.
chapters.coreMove: Locate the desire or comparison disturbing your peace and release the demand that reality change first.
chapters.commonMisread: The weak version becomes positive thinking, gratitude slogans, wellness mood hacks, or the claim that happiness is easy if you choose it.

chapters.title: Saving Yourself
chapters.sourcePressure: The source insists that experts cannot make you healthy, calm, rich, or free. It ties being yourself, caring for health, diet, exercise, meditation, growth, expectations, anger, employment, and uncontrolled thinking to personal responsibility.
chapters.coreMove: Stop outsourcing responsibility and turn the next neglected area of life into a chosen priority you actually protect.
chapters.commonMisread: The weak version becomes a generic self-care checklist, fitness routine, diet plan, or inspirational self-reliance speech without the hard priority tradeoff.

chapters.title: Philosophy
chapters.sourcePressure: The source asks old questions about meaning, values, rational Buddhism, evolution, honesty, peer relationships, anger, death, and the present. Its pressure is not to provide doctrine, but to teach tested, self-owned philosophy.
chapters.coreMove: Hold a large question long enough to separate inherited doctrine from values you can test and live by.
chapters.commonMisread: The weak version becomes abstract life-purpose prose, spiritual generalities, or a summary of philosophical positions instead of a practical inquiry into meaning, values, verification, and presence.

chapters.title: Naval’s Recommended Reading
chapters.sourcePressure: The source presents reading as curiosity-led connoisseurship: theory, concepts, nonfiction, philosophy, science fiction, blogs, and other sources that build mental models. The pressure is to turn a list into a reading practice, not a catalog.
chapters.coreMove: Choose reading by live curiosity and mental-model yield instead of finishing lists for self-improvement status.
chapters.commonMisread: The weak version becomes a book recommendation roundup, summary of famous titles, or advice to read more without showing how to follow curiosity, abandon bad fits, and build taste.
